quotes.text: The core line is still the simplest one. Chat is for discovery. Agents are for execution. Confuse the two and you automate ambiguity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the episode's central design principle in a memorable line.

quotes.text: Prompts can shape tone. Prompts can reduce some ambiguity. Prompts can nudge behavior, but prompts cannot manufacture a control plane that doesn't exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why prompt engineering alone cannot fix agent governance.

quotes.text: If you can't predict the action path, you can't govern it. If you can't govern it, you can't scale it. If you can't scale it, your ROI is a one time demo artifact.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear chain of reasoning linking determinism to governance, scale and ROI.

quotes.text: And in enterprise systems, surface area is destiny because agents don't amplify your best process. They amplify your weakest governance path.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that agents scale existing governance weaknesses.

quotes.text: This wasn't a Copilot Studio success story. It was an architecture success story implemented with Copilot Studio. Same platform, same connectors, same models, different sequence, different constraints, different definition of done.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows that success depends on architecture and build order, not the platform.

takeaways: Copilot agents fail when conversation carries the workflow; use chat for discovery and parameter collection and push execution into deterministic flows and APIs.
Every action-capable agent needs intent contracts, an explicit identity model, bounded knowledge, narrow tool contracts and a system of record for evidence.
Run agents as a governed portfolio with environments, DLP, release gates, regression tests and metrics such as intervention rate and determinism instead of session counts.
hook: Most Copilot Studio agents look great in the demo and quietly lose trust in production. This episode is for architects and IT leaders building action-capable agents, and explains the contracts, identity, orchestration and governance needed to make agent outcomes repeatable, auditable and safe to scale.
